Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing and issuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer; and David Patel, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2023. We delivered strong results, driven by robust gross written premiums growth across our lines of business, elevated investment income yields, favorable trends in customer acquisition costs, solid realized gains alongside improving unrealized positions in our portfolio, and strategic capital deployment into high-return opportunities. Our focus on digital transformation and profitable growth continues to yield positive outcomes.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $620 million, or $2.10 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included double-digit GWP expansion, higher reinvestment yields on our float, and disciplined expense management. Our combined ratio was 95.8%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. Investment income for the quarter was $1.2 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with $4.2 billion in deployable capital.

Let me start by walking through our top-line momentum, focusing on gross written premiums growth by line of business. Consolidated GWP rose 9.2% year-over-year to $14.8 billion, achieving our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth excluding catastrophe impacts. This significantly outpaced the P&C industry average of 6.8% per AM Best, thanks to disciplined pricing, high retention rates, and expansion into high-margin areas.

In personal lines, our largest segment at 42% of total GWP, we posted 7.1% growth to $6.2 billion. Auto premiums increased 4.8%, supported by 6% new business from our DriveSafe telematics program, which now covers 28% of policies and uses AI for better risk selection, achieving 89% retention above JD Power benchmarks. We navigated competitive pressures in California and Florida despite 12% repair cost inflation. Homeowners and other personal lines surged 12.3%, driven by 8% rate hikes, 5% policy count growth, and careful cat exposure management—we non-renewed 15,000 high-risk Florida policies post-Hurricane Ian, redirecting to Texas and the Midwest. Parametric products for wildfire and flood added $250 million in new GWP through Swiss Re partnerships. U.S. personal lines grew 8.2%, Europe 3.5% amid UK FCA pricing remedies, and Asia-Pacific 15% via China WeChat micro-insurance bundles.

Commercial lines delivered 11.5% growth to $4.9 billion, or 33% of the portfolio, with a stellar 92.4% combined ratio beating peers like Travelers. Middle market and SME grew 10.2% on 9% rate gains and 7% volume in workers' comp and general liability, powered by our GLASS platform for 20% faster ML-driven quotes. We gained share in construction and manufacturing, adding cyber endorsements to 65% of policies amid ransomware threats. Large corporate jumped 14.8%, with D&O up 22% from IPO slowdowns and ESG litigation, hitting 92% retention via risk consulting. U.S. commercial led at 13%, Europe 9% despite German slowdowns, and LatAm 18% through our Mapfre Brazil JV for agribusiness amid El Niño.

Specialty and reinsurance shone with 13.7% growth to $2.7 billion, 18% of GWP, at a 55% attritional loss ratio versus industry 62%. Quota shares and excess-of-loss drove marine cargo up 16% from Red Sea issues and aviation 20% post-Boeing woes. Cyber added $400 million, up 25%, with parametric business interruption triggers akin to Munich Re's. Reinsurance assumed rose 12% after our $1.2 billion cat bond issuance reduced retrocession needs. APAC led at 22% in marine and typhoon covers, North America in casualty clash.

Life and health annuities grew 8.4% to $1.0 billion, 7% of total, led by 15% in fixed indexed annuities via SecureFuture, capturing 10% retirement market share per LIMRA as rates hit 5.2%. Health supplements rose 4% despite Medicare pressures.

This GWP strength reflects our Profitable Growth 2025 strategy: 60/40 rate-to-volume split, 75% organic. We've rolled out GenAI for claims triage, cutting times 30% for dynamic pricing; closed a $450 million UK MGA acquisition adding 5% specialty run-rate; optimized reinsurance at 28% ceded ratio for 25% equity-like ROE; and priced for $50 billion industry cat losses per RMS. Ex-FX, full-year GWP guides to 9-11%, personal lines mid-teens in H2. Our balance sheet is robust with $8.5 billion liquidity and 250% statutory capital surplus.

Shifting to investments, our income yield hit 4.1% annualized for the quarter, up 90 basis points year-over-year from 3.2% and 20 basis points sequentially from Q2's 3.9%. This is our best since Q1 2008, fueled by rates and management on $115 billion average assets—our float swelled from P&C premium gains in auto and commercial multi-peril. Investment income jumped 28% to $1.2 billion.

Fixed income, 72% of our $120 billion portfolio, yielded 4.5% book yield, up from 3.4%, with 45% investment-grade corporates at 5.2% new buys amid 110 bps spreads over Treasuries. The 10-year averaged 4.3%; agency MBS and RMBS at 18% yielded over 5% with lower prepay risk. Equities, 12%, returned 6.8% with 2.4% dividends from S&P Dividend Aristocrats and financials like Chubb peers. Alternatives at 16% included 5.1% REITs and 4% ILS for uncorrelated returns.

Trailing 12-month yield rose from 3.0% to 3.9%, beating Barclays Aggregate by 60 bps via active duration at 5.4 years, matching liabilities with under 2% ALM gaps. Credit is top-tier: 92% IG, A- average, 0.1% non-performers. U.S. fixed (65%) yielded 5.4% new money; Europe (20%) 3.2% pivoting to UK gilts at 4.1%; Asia-Pac (10%) 4.8% on JGBs and semis; EM capped at 3% in quasi-sovs.

We're not chasing yield: high-yield <5%, ORSA stress-tested. ESG screens 25% new fixed income SFDR 8/9 compliant via BlackRock/PIMCO, no yield sacrifice. AI optimizer boosts yield 15 bps with convexity hedges. Post-SVB, banks trimmed to 8%, favoring insurers and cat bonds with Swiss Re.

Full-year yield guides 4.0%, Q4 4.2-4.3% at Fed pause; 2024 4.5%+ on steepening curve, aiding 14% ROE. Monitoring duration and 40% recession odds.

On investment results, net realized gains were $285 million, up 12% QoQ and 28% YoY, from fixed sales harvesting post-banking crisis rallies. Unrealized net loss narrowed to $2.8 billion in AOCI (78% AFS), up $450 million QoQ, via duration trim to 5.8 years matching 6.1-year liabilities.

Realized: $210 million fixed (15% QoQ), $45 million equities (financials/tech), $30 million alternatives private credit; losses $15 million EM repositioning. Yield 2.1% annualized, on 2.3% FY guide. Unrealized: $3.1 billion fixed losses offset by $300 million equities; short-duration (25%) gained $620 million.

Net investment income ex-gains grew 8% to $1.75 billion at 4.8% reinvestments. AOCI pressured BVPS to $68.50, down 4% like MetLife/Prudential.

North America (65%): $185 million realized IG/RMBS/munis >4%. Europe (20%): €1.2 billion unrealized on Bunds/gilts, $40 million peripheral sales. Asia/EM (15%): $60 million Aussie/Indo gains, losses from China property—capped 5%, pivot to 7.5% INR bonds.

ALM advanced with Aladdin Monte Carlo for +200bps shocks; $2.5 billion derivatives hedge 40% gap, cutting volatility 25%. Alternatives at 18% (target 20%) via Blackstone BREIT/Brookfield infra at 6-8% IRRs. Q4 realized $220-250 million; unrealized peak/recover as rates plateau 4.0-4.5%. Annuities sales up 22% on higher crediting. 15% new fixed ESG/SFDR green bonds mitigate P&C climate risks.

Book yield +110 bps YoY, Sharpe 0.85, investment ROA 2.4%, supporting 10-12% 2024 EPS growth.

Customer acquisition costs, or CAC, remain a P&L highlight amid softening premiums and competition from Progressive, Allstate, Lemonade, and Root. CAC is fully loaded: marketing, commissions, onboarding, G&A overhead per new annualized premium in force—aligned with Bain/McKinsey benchmarks.

Q3 blended CAC fell 14% YoY to $428 per policy from $498, 5% sequentially from $450, below $500-550 peer averages per AM Best. Digital CAC dropped 22% to $265 via InsureAI lead scoring at 78% qualification.

Personal lines (62% new): 18% drop to $312; auto $285 on telematics with GM/Ford APIs like Snapshot, 31% UBI conversions; homeowners $420 via IoT bundles. Commercial (25%): $2,450 flat, 9% cut in SMB embedded APIs with Shopify/QuickBooks for cyber/liability. Life/health (13%): 8% to $1,120 on Google campaigns, CPL $45.

U.S. (68% new API): $410, 16% down post-Dodd-Frank, telematics beating Prop 103. Europe (20%): $480, 9% drop despite GDPR/IDD; UK motor 12% via aggregators, French/German agent-heavy. Asia-Pac (12%): $620 up 3% vs. Ping An, but Indonesia halved to $180 via Gojek.

Digital First, Agent Augmented: 35% of $450 million marketing to programmatic (5.2x ROAS), app AR visualization, Oscar alliances—LTV/CAC 4.8x from 4.1x, auto LTV 62 months. Q4 $415 CAC via GenAI chatbots 40% self-serve lift, Chime/Revolut embeds. LTV +7% to $2,100 on inflation/retention.

Finally, our capital deployment strategy underpins long-term shareholder value. We ended Q3 with $4.2 billion deployable capital, up 12% YoY, from 95.8% ex-cat combined ratio and $1.8 billion 12-month cash flow—strong vs. peers facing cat losses and hardening reinsurance.

Framework: (1) organic high-return, (2) bolt-on M&A, (3) shareholder returns. Target 14-16% ROE cycle, 22% leverage, 620% RBC vs. 500% target.

Organic: $1.2 billion (30% capital). P&C parametric up 45% YoY to $450 million run-rate; Zenith ClimateShield with Munich Re for SMEs in Florida/Gulf at 25% attachment. Life/health $300 million embedded into Chime/Robinhood—$120 million GWP pilot at 88% LR. Asia $400 million health reinsurance at 15-20% CAGR; Europe 12% D&O in $50 billion cyber-soft market. Tech $500 million: GenAI automates 40% underwriting, expense ratio -150 bps to 28.5%; IBM blockchain cuts workers' comp claims 45-to-12 days, fraud -22%.

Acquisitions: $800 million YTD vs. $2-3 billion pipeline. $650 million CyberGuard Analytics accretive $0.15 EPS, cyber GWP $2.1-to-$3.8 billion vs. $10.5 billion global claims; 200 bps margins by Q4 2024. $150 million Brazil AgroSegura for LatAm parametric, 8% premiums to 15% trend, 18% IRR <96% CR earn-outs. Pipeline: cyber/climate, $100 billion U.S. MGU, Australia bushfires.

Shareholder returns: dividend +8% to $0.65, 2.8% yield; $900 million repurchases at 12x fwd earnings vs. Travelers 14x; $1.5 billion left, buy below 1.4x BV.

10% organic growth targets pricing discipline vs. 6% claims inflation; 11% 5-year BVPS CAGR beats S&P Insurance by 400 bps.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines segment. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced parametric triggers and AI-driven modeling that have kept our attritional loss ratios low.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for issuing questions: press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the GWP growth outlook, particularly in specialty lines?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, David. Absolutely. Our specialty and reinsurance book grew 13.7% this quarter, and we're positioned for continued strength. The cyber franchise alone added $400 million, reflecting demand for parametric triggers amid rising ransomware. With our recent cat bond issuance and MGA acquisition, we expect this segment to drive outsized contributions, targeting mid-teens growth in 2024 while maintaining that 55% loss ratio edge over the industry.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of the higher-for-longer rate environment on your investment portfolio?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, Emily. The rate environment has been a significant tailwind, pushing our yield to 4.1% and net investment income up 28%. We've captured this through laddering into 5.2% corporates and 5% MBS, with duration at 5.4 years matching liabilities. Realized gains hit $285 million from tactical sales, and unrealized losses are narrowing. For 2024, we see 4.5%+ yields supporting ROE expansion, though we're hedged against early cuts via derivatives overlaying 40% of gaps.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Thanks. What is the expected impact of evolving climate regulations on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Robert. Climate regs are front and center, but our strategy is resilient. We've non-renewed high-risk exposures post-Ian, launched ClimateShield parametrics with 25% attachment, and integrated ESG into risk selection. In homeowners and commercial, we're using AI and blockchain for precise modeling, keeping combined ratios at 95.8% ex-cat. Regs like EU SFDR actually align with our parametric and reinsurance optimizations, positioning us to grow profitably in high-peril zones.

Operator: Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Anna Patel: Good morning. On capital deployment, any updates to the M&A pipeline?

Michael Rivera: Hi Anna. Our $2-3 billion pipeline remains active, focused on cyber, climate, and distribution. CyberGuard is already accretive, expanding GWP meaningfully, and AgroSegura diversifies LatAm. We're eyeing U.S. MGU consolidation like Ryan Specialty and Australia tuck-ins for bushfire parallels to California. All deals target 18% IRR with CR hurdles, balancing organic tech spends like our $500 million AI/blockchain push.

Operator: Our final question today comes from Mark Thompson with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson: Good morning. How are CAC trends influencing LTV and retention?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, Mark. CAC efficiency at $428, down 14% YoY, boosts LTV/CAC to 4.8x. Digital channels at $265 CAC via InsureAI, telematics conversions up 31%, and embedded pilots with fintechs extend policy life to 62 months. Q4 guides $415 with GenAI quoting, countering ad fatigue via first-party data—retention at 89-92% across lines supports scalable growth.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
